title: Fantastic
review:
Inception is easily one of the most complex movies that I have ever watched in my entire life. It is apparent right off the bat how much thinking and effort must have been put in by writer and director Christopher Nolan in order to build such a structured plot. Nolan really did a phenomenal job in creating a film that really stimulates the audience to think. However, if you aren't constantly thinking and keeping up with what's going on in the film then you will lose touch with what is happening in the film in the beat of an eye. If focus is lost for even a few seconds that could leave the viewer lost and confused just because the plot is always being built upon and added to in some way throughout every second of the movie. One thing that might be harder than keeping track of the movie is explaining what it's about to others. As soon as I was finished watching the movie I tried to convince one of my friends to watch it by explaining what it's about, but I quickly realized that there's no way in doing Inception justice by trying to explain the plot and I just told her to go watch the movie. A lot of people I have talked to have told me that they had to watch the movie two or three times to be able to comprehend what the hell is going on.

With that being said, if the viewer is actually able to keep track of the plot it is awesome to see how the original plot is constantly added to and modified to bring it to the level of complexity that it holds. The starting scene in the movie is actually brought from towards the ending where the main character Dom is in an unending dream world know as limbo and he is trying to find the man that will eventually lead him back to his family. The rest of the movie after that scene explains how he got there. The movie goes in depth explaining the idea of invading other people's dreams and using that skill to manipulate them. This idea of traveling through other people's dreams and looking at how the different levels of dreams work and how these dreams relate back to the victims beliefs and experiences in real life is really just a mind blowing concept and is an awesome idea to think about. It probably took Chris Nolan years to get the storyline ready and finalized just looking at how interrelated some of the aspects of the plot are to each other. The complexity of the plot wasn't the only part that made this the great movie that it is though, the execution in the acting also definitely added to the movie's splendor. Leonardo DiCaprio played his role for Dom perfectly just like he does for any movie that he's in, and it is easy to see how much thought the director put into picking actors for the specific roles that he needed because pretty much every other actor fills their role perfectly even though they aren't exactly the biggest names in the industry. I think this is a very underrated quality in actors in Hollywood because an actor should not be chosen for a role based on how much weight their name carries but more so on the basis of how well their characteristics display what you want to be displayed for the character that they are playing. I think it's obvious that Nolan and his crew realize this and took it into accounting when doing auditions.

Inception definitely did a great job in bringing a new and original idea for a movie to the table and certainly reached its potential with the help of a great execution from the cast, directing, and other crew members. It was the first truly good, mind stimulating, and involving movie that I have seen in a while, and it gave me hope that maybe modern day movies aren't as bad as I thought they were and Hollywood still has the ability to entertain me.

Principal photography began in Tokyo on June 19, 2009, with the scene where Saito first hires Cobb during a helicopter flight over the city.

The production moved to the United Kingdom and shot in a converted airship hangar in Cardington, Bedfordshire, north of London. There, the hotel bar set which tilted 30 degrees was built. A hotel corridor was also constructed by Guy Hendrix Dyas, the production designer, Chris Corbould, the special effects supervisor, and Wally Pfister, the director of photography; it rotated a full 360 degrees to create the effect of alternate directions of gravity for scenes set during the second level of dreaming, where dream-sector physics become chaotic. The idea was inspired by a technique used in Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968). Nolan said, "I was interested in taking those ideas, techniques, and philosophies and applying them to an action scenario". The filmmakers originally planned to make the hallway only 40 ft (12 m) long, but as the action sequence became more elaborate, the hallway's length grew to 100 ft (30 m). The corridor was suspended along eight large concentric rings that were spaced equidistantly outside its walls and powered by two massive electric motors.

title: A film to twist your idea of reality with amazing results
review: We all know our imagination when used can come up some of the most amazing and wonderful things, things that can bring a smile to our face or even make us cringe in fear, the good thing about using our imagination though is it is us who is using it and in that way it is us who controls exactly what happens, the same thing in our dreams as well. We are the ones who control our dreams if we know how. Leonardo DiCaprio (Basketball Diaries, Titanic) plays Dom Cobb a man who with his partner Arthur played by Joseph Gordon Levitt (Mysterious Skin, Stop-Loss) are "extractors", people who can enter the dreams and sub conscious of the unwilling through some military experiment and gather information with their contract none the wiser. The duo is hired by Japanese business man Saito played by Ken Watanabe ( Memoirs of a Geisha, Batman Begins) to enter the sub conscious of Robert Fischer Jr played by Cillian Murphy (Batman Begins, Breakfast on Pluto) and get him to dissolve his dead father's company. If Cobb and his team are successful Saito will ensure the murder charge that Cobb is currently being hunted for (murdering his wife) is dropped and he can go back and be with his two kids once again. Cobb assembles a team ready to enter the 3 levels of Roberts's subconscious whilst he travels from Sydney to Los Angeles with the corpse of his father Inception is a film that if you look away for a second you are utterly lost, miss that one important sentence and you'll be left scratching your head wondering what the hell is actually going on. Is it a film that can hold your attention for the entirety or do you lose interest here and there and wonder what to buy in the supermarket once you leave the cinema? For me it was amazing, so far-fetched and over convoluted, so much bullshit and crazy ideas, so much imagination and wonder all in one very messy and crisscrossed package. I have seen this movie about 3 times now and it still confuses me, in saying that though I do still love it as well. Every time I have watched it I have gotten more and more out of it. I believe it to be the type of film where if two people sitting in the same cinema met after the film to have a coffee and debrief neither of them would agree on the same thing to which they had just seen anyway, both of them would have seen exactly the same thing but come to two very different conclusions. I believe personally that's exactly what Nolan wants from his audience with this film, he wants us (the audience) to walk away and tell each other our own ideas and theories and walk away totally bewildered. For that it works and it works so very well. The scenes set up in some of this movie are beyond imagination, there is one very amazing scene with Joseph Gordon Levitt's character that gives me tingles just thinking about it. Nolan is a very very smart man and no doubt has very big things to bring to the cinematic world. The ending by far is one of the most significant in the film I have my own ideas as I'm sure you will as well. I don't believe this is a film you would enjoy with anyone under 18 and then again even those over 18 without imagination and the ability to escape into a reality of complete amazement won't enjoy it either. Inception gets 4.5 BanShee Screams out of 5 only because there is still so much to it I want to understand and can't without getting Christopher Nolan to sit down and break it down for me even though I'm aware of how much that will kill the entire film for me.

title: If you rate this with one star, you're exactly as stupid as Mr. Nolan thinks you are!
review:
My inspiration for this review is another review on this movie called "You're not as stupid as Mr. Nolan believes you are". Why? Because you believe somebody is trying to sell their product and along with that fool you? I don't think it's that simple! Here's why:

1. You're exactly as stupid as mr. Nolan thinks you are if you decide to stop watching after the first 5 minutes of the movie. I agree though that the beginning is nothing special, but at least give it a try and then you'll see what was about that beginning.

2. You're exactly as stupid as mr. Nolan thinks you are if you try to figure out what is it with that dream machine. It's a Science Fiction people! There must be things that will not make sense. This is the Sci-fi world!

3. You're exactly as stupid as mr. Nolan thinks you are if you compare this movie to Matrix. I'm not a fan of that movie, but let's just say that is not the most logical movie ever. While here everything that happens in the dream world follows a familiar pattern of real life dreams. The way you get kicked out of it, how real it seems, and the idea of all possibilities.

4. You're exactly as stupid as mr. Nolan thinks you are if you criticize this movie for it's theories about dream share. That never happened in real world, it's science fiction, again, that's why here we should give the credit to the director and embrace the way the shared dreams work.

5. You're exactly as stupid as mr. Nolan thinks you are if you believe that he remained in the dream. Now i'll not explain the whole movie at this point, but let's just say that reality was the only place he could go. Remember he was sedated in the reality, and Saito died in the first dream that's why he went to limbo in the first place, to get Saito back from there. So Cobb going after Saito meant that he wouldn't feel the kick from the second dream resulting in him not waking up in the water-filled car from the first dream, so he died in the first dream. So even if he was shot by Saito in limbo and returned to the first dream he was dead there and had to wake up in reality. Not convinced? Go check the cast and see that there are two sets of children one with James 20 months and Phillipa 3 years and one with James 3 years and Phillipa 5 years. Yet another proof that if you rate this movie with 1 you didn't payed any attention at all to see if his children were older in reality and if he was wearing the wedding ring in reality or not, and so on...

In conclusion I say only this even if I could have written a poem about how amazing was the score the cinematography or the visual effects, I'll say only this: This is one of a kind movie that keeps the most of it's viewers on the edge of their seat with a brilliant idea and excellent storytelling.

The main idea of this movie is that the team is like a movie cast(director, producer, ex producer, visual effects man, screenplay and lead actor) trying to deliver a good show to impress Fischer(the audience) and in the same time to plant an idea into his mind.

So going back to the final scene. Was it all a dream? Of course! It's a movie isn't it?

title: A Real "Inception"
review:
It takes a highly creative mind to consistently keep thinking out- of-the-box. It takes a compelling story-teller to make you comprehend those thoughts. And it takes a lot of hard-work, dedication and perseverance to convert that story to reel. Put it all together and you have a gist of what went into creating "Inception". And the results speak for themselves!

A seamless, "many-layered" film, "Inception" is on one hand a dazzling extravaganza of Science and Technology and on the other, an emotional drama, with the internal conflicts of the lead characters threading through the scenes and binding the entire plot together.

This film is no exception to Nolan's unique ability of non-linear story-telling, and it takes a little getting used to. However, once you have an idea of what's going on, you cannot help but marvel at the grandeur and brilliance of it all.

Leonardo DiCaprio excelled as the highly-talented but incapacitated mastermind of the group. Ellen Page was right up to the mark playing the young, fresh and at times irritatingly inquisitive "newbie" of the group. Tom Hardy and Joseph Gordon-Levitt's on-screen chemistry was fun to watch. Marion Cotillard and Cilian Murphy had more or less one-dimensional roles to play and they played them okay.

Overall, "Inception" is definitely worth watching, and then watching again, and again. It will make you ponder deeper about the realms of the human mind in all senses of the phrase. True to its name, this is a real "inception" of Nolan's and has the power to change the way we think.

We have to trust him that he can lead us through, because much of the time we're lost and disoriented. Nolan must have rewritten this story time and again, finding that every change had a ripple effect down through the whole fabric.Like the hero of that film, the viewer of "Inception" is adrift in time and experience. And what if you're inside another man's dream? How does your dream time synch with his? What do you really know?

title: Nolan's and Zimmer's Masterpiece
review:
Inception constantly invites you to marvel in expertise, both that of the characters and the filmmakers themselves-- Wally Pfister's camera work, Hans Zimmer's score, Chris Corbould's visual effects are all unparalleled and utilized beautifully. The story has tremendous emotional payoff near the end, and there is great satisfaction in merely watching the team come together as equals, but it's hard not to wish for something more from the smaller characters. Gordon-Levitt, Page and particularly Hardy make strong impacts in their limited roles, as does Michael Caine in what amounts to a glorified cameo, but for the large part they are merely eloquent pieces of a particularly impressive machinery.

The movies often seem to come from the recycling bin these days: Sequels, remakes, franchises. "Inception" does a difficult thing. It is wholly original, cut from new cloth, and yet structured with action movie basics so it feels like it makes more sense than (quite possibly) it does. Christopher Nolan reinvented "Batman." This time he isn't reinventing anything. Yet few directors will attempt to recycle "Inception." I think when Nolan left the labyrinth, he threw away the map.

'Inception' is a stunning score. Expectations are high when Hans Zimmer is attached to a project. He has delivered many of the great scores of the last twenty years. The pieces often take their time to tell their stories. This adds to the tension of the music. There is so much emotion in this score that it is impossible to ignore it even when playing in the background. But be careful. When you finish the album, take a look around you. Play 'Non, Je ne Regrette Rien' in your ears one more time. Because hey, you never know. Pleasant dreams.

And if there's a song that I must talk about... 'Time'. It is, without question, the most important, most beautiful and most evocative piece in the score (and personally the best piece I have ever heard in my life). It begins simply – a piano plays chords as a throbbing beat hums behind it. The passengers wake up on the plane. However, despite the success, despite the rescue and despite reality returning, there really is only one story at work – Cobb's return and absolution. So, the piece holds its tension. This tension, however, has changed. People are not falling off bridges, or hanging in elevator shafts, or even living to old age in the blink of an eye. This is about one man coming home to his children. The piece becomes a theme that is stated, repeated and played in variation. The emotion it stirs as you walk with Cobb, first through the airport, then through security and finally into his home is indescribable. The clear ringing of the horns as his victory is realised could only be described as truly epic. It reminds the listener of Zimmer's earlier work, particularly Gladiator, in tone. The piece then fades down as he sees his two children from behind, as he has so many times through the film. He places the spinning top on the table. The other instruments fall away completely now and the piano is left playing single notes, no longer chords. Everything has fallen by the wayside. His children turn to face him and they smile. When the strings end and the camera pans away from this reunion, the score gives us one last nod as the music flips up into a sharp crescendo. The top is still spinning, with a small wobble.

All in all, Inception is probably the best movie I have watched in my entire life.

title: Nolan's vision is still breathtaking
review:
As much as I can't deny that in more recent viewings, Inception hasn't wowed me as much as the first time (but then again few movies do). Still, in one of my latest revisits, the movie continues to grab my full attention whether it's with smartly written dialog or exciting action scenes. Plus I still believe that DiCaprio deserved a bit more recognition in his role as it's one of great emotional depth.

So in Inception we are introduced to a world in which dream-sharing is possible and procedures like extraction are the norm in the espionage game. Cobb (DiCaprio) seems to be the biggest player, but now he is faced with a choice, as a wealthy energy mogul named Saito (Watanabe) promises him an opportunity to stop running and go back home to the U.S. The catch? He must perform Inception on the subject, or in more known terms, implant an idea in the subconscious. Christopher Nolan has directed one the best movies of the genre for me. A complex idea that is shown to the audience by fantastic visuals and asks some pertinent questions, Inception allows you to be entertained but also mentally aware of what's going on. It is a blockbuster movie, there's no question there. However it's one that offers a unique story that plays out at a fast pace and with ideas that will certainly be discussed after the movie finishes.

Inception is without a doubt still a great movie. It's been 4 years since its release, so understandably the hype has died down, as has the discussion of the movie's plot. Some of us still love it, others have been let down in repeat viewings, while some still claim the movie is flawed and not smart. Personally I believe it's a masterpiece within the genre. As a general movie? Well that's a discussion for another time. My final advice is whether you end up liking it not, do yourself a favor and watch this movie if you still haven't. It's unmissable.

Rating: 10/10

title: Very good, though with a few holes. Needs to be seen more than once to be fully enjoyed.
review: I hesitate to give this an integer rating because I really would give it a 9.5 but each roundable integers are either too high or low for my liking. This is a movie that can get a lot of hatred from people that don't like confusing movies, and you can see more about my opinion on that topic in my Pirates 3 review. But in terms of this movie, I would say, watch it carefully without trying to understand every detail and rule of the dreams, because that isn't really going to work. If you're okay with seeing movies multiple times, try to absorb it in a few elements per viewing. If you absolutely refuse to see movies more than once, I would recommend that you not watch this movie because anyone you ask will tell you that it's too confusing to absorb in one viewing. If you pay attention, there are a couple of holes that you can find in the rules of the dream and how well they are followed, but I did not find that any of these detracted very much. If you don't have time to watch the whole movie all at once, leave off at the scene where Cobb and his team are about to go into the dream with Fischer on the plane. It is not a good idea to stop watching the movie during the last hour. This is the type of movie that has two elements to it: the idea and the story. Both are done well in this movie, unlike in some movies like Hunger Games or Divergent, where I feel that the overemphasis on the story detracts from the concept being presented. I've observed that a lot of people seem to think that the plot is about a dream within a dream, but it's really more about the idea illustrated in the title: the planting of an idea. The way that the team of Cobb, Saito, Arthur, Eames, Ariadne, and Yusuf work to alter Fischer's perception of his father is really interesting and the element you should probably focus on most the first time you watch it. I have seen other reviews that complain about a lack of character development, but I think that this only holds true for Yusuf, who is sort of just recruited for his abilities with chemicals. I suppose that's why they leave him in the first level. The action is pretty good too, especially the zero gravity part in the hotel with Arthur. Still, I would not recommend this movie to someone seeking strictly action, though there is a lot of that in it. The background story with Mal and Cobb is pretty good, though sometimes it can be hard for first time viewers to understand what aspects of it are important to Cobb's current plight. For people interested in a way to interpret dreams, this isn't the movie for you, nor is it a terribly good representation of real dreams. Then again, it's kind of hard to cinematically depict an actual dream in such a way that an average audience can understand. So, I would say that this is a movie to watch if you like other movies by Christopher Nolan (and ones with phenomenal scores by Hans Zimmer). It is kind of similar to The Matrix and The Prestige. But overall I would say it's a very good and interesting film that I would recommend to anyone who likes a movie that is well done and well thought out.

title: Brilliant movie!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
review: Dom Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio) doesn't steal things, he steals ideas. In the world of corporate espionage, Cobb is the ultimate weapon. But even weapons have their weakness, and when Cobb loses everything, he's forced to embark on one final mission in a desperate quest for redemption. This time, Cobb won't be harvesting an idea, but sowing one. Should he and his team of specialists succeed, they will have discovered a new frontier in the art of psychic espionage. They've planned everything to perfection, and they have all the tools to get the job done. Their mission is complicated, however, by the sudden appearance of a malevolent foe that seems to know exactly what they're up to, and precisely how to stop them.

title: Your mind is the scene of crime?
review:
Nolan attained cult status in Hollywood owing to his master screenplay and narrative in movies like Memento(2002). And his vision of the Batman series was a spectacle that both the fans and non-fans of the series' enjoyed alike. Now Nolan through his imagination has brought us a journey into the world of imagination itself. Inception is about the world of the dream and how to hack into your dreams as well as others.

Central to the plot is a piece of tech, developed by the army, which enables people to share dreams. This is what Cobb(Dicaprio) and his associates use to commit mental heists. Cobb lands a job that needs him, not to steal an idea from someone's mind, but to place one there instead and make it seem self-generated by the subject himself. You can do that? This has never been done before but Cobb needs to do this to get back to his children.

This movie is not of the sit-back, relax and enjoy genre. It is fast paced and does not wait for you to understand what just happened. Unless you are totally alert, you will get lost. You have to keep track of dreams within dreams and it is not abundantly clear how things actually work in the dream world.

But the ten years that Nolan has supposedly put into the film definitely paid off. He masterfully communicates his vision with the audience. The plot has a lot of gaps which the viewer himself has to fill to make the narrative congruent. So this is definitely going to stay on your mind for a while even after you leave the theater.

The movie is visually stunning. The CG is seamless and top notch. All the actors render laudable performances. My favorite definitely though is Eames(Tom Hardy). He is a professional thief and an expert forger and extremely cool.

But Nolan is no expert at directing fight scenes. They do tend to wear you out as they are not very exciting in themselves. The movie definitely has quite a number of inconsistencies too. This surely must have been due to the short window of time in which Nolan had to present everything about this new world from conception to conclusion.

All in all this is a must watch for people who want to challenge their intellect. And as I've said before this not for one's with a faint heart as you might find yourself bored or completely confused unless you are extremely alert.

title: Inception
review:
Title: Inception

Condensed Storyline: A thief who steals corporate information by using a dream machine gets contracted to do the biggest job of his life.

Notable Acting: I have a feeling Christopher Nolan loved the cast of this movie so much that he used a handful of them for his next movie 'The Dark Knight Rises' But regardless, this movie has A-list actors who all take a portion of the film and carry it along in a way which doesn't feel force, but feels like everyone is getting their own amounts of screen time. I didn't really care about half of the characters, but the movie made me sort of care about them, that is impressive for a movie to do.

Noticeable Camera work: This movie may be good with how it is visually filmed, but god does it have a lot of filming continuity errors. I generally do not notice continuity errors, but they seemed to stick out in this movie. This movie is a fan of rotational camera work along with some size play included into the mixture

Graphics: The CGI in the movie is amazingly mixed into the visual effects, such as the rotating hall way, that was all practical effects, the scenes in the snow and similar things are CGI, but are so well done that you do have to question at first if they are CGI or are just very good practical effects.

Overall Feel: A simple way to describe this movie is, it is the Matrix of 2010. It blends stunning CGI with amazing practical effects. But the movie is quite complex for a movie and does require a thinking active audience, an passive person watching for the first time will likely have no clue what is going on. This movie is visually stunning, with a half decent plot and enjoyable actors.

title: A Great Movie- Often Misunderstood
review:
To keep it short, sweet and to the point, let's not go over every painstaking detail of why this movie was clever and interesting. Christopher Nolan is a brilliant director, and I don't believe he received quite enough credit for this film. At face value, it's fairly easy to follow and allows the lowest common denominator to enjoy a story of love, loss, and dream-poking ridiculousness. Dig a bit deeper into it, and you see that Nolan had big things in mind. The most common argument to arise from this movie is that of whether or not the movie itself is a dream because of the scene at the end- the top bobbling but not falling. This is a smokescreen, as many have discussed before me. Listen to the children in the background- turn on the subtitles if you are unable to hear them clearly as it can be difficult with some sound systems. Once you hear their input (which I will not spoon-feed), you can then make some logical conclusions about the rest of the film. You can track the use (or in this case, misuse) of totems, the failure of continuity between "going a level up" when you are killed in a certain level of a dream, etc.

Stylistically, and creatively, this film was a feat and should be on lists for best film of the year- definitely not the most well written, directed, or acted film- but its clever storytelling and intentional misdirection is something of note. There are obvious mistakes in timing when arranging the kick on the bridge, as well as several other goofs along those lines, but if viewers hope to glean more from this film, you need only re-watch it and pay close attention (notice how in Mumbasa the attackers come at Cobb from out of nowhere similar to projections).

All in all, I very much enjoy this film, and believe it can be a fun watch for both the critical and casual viewer.

I found it to be too clever by half, far too complicated and definitely too long. Special effects were very impressive but there were not many of them and they did not save the film.

title: No doubt this film could be one of the greatest sci-fi, action movies ever made.
review:
Inception. What a masterpiece. Christopher Nolan has really outdone himself with this insane concept of people sharing the same dream space and exploring the idea of a 'dream within a dream'. With Leonardo DiCaprio as the protagonist, Cobb, he puts on a stunning performance, which leaves you speechless and in absolute awe of his uncanny film talent.

The movie uses layers of dreams to build up the structure of the movie's plot line, transitioning between each one at alternate stages. With the idea being somewhat unrealistic, the film easily makes up for this through attracting viewers by ensuring that they are eager to uncover the mystery of its non-linear plot line.

DiCaprio has a unique acting style that he commonly uses in all of his movies. Throughout Inception though, he slotted comfortably into the life of Cobb and conveyed his life both outstandingly and consistently. The way he expresses pain and emotional difficulties is very believable and he connects with the audiences while doing so.

Nolan has put in an exceptional effort in the construction of his film. I recommend it over most films of its genre but to properly gain the most out of it and to completely understand the plot line, the viewer must be engaged constantly. It is worth seeing it twice, almost three times to grasp its general concept. This film's themes are also quite complex and thus, attract audiences who enjoy such themes. Personally, I would rate this film a solid 10 out of 10 for the exceptional effort put in by Nolan and for the elaboration on the central idea of the film, people sharing the same dream space.

title: This is a review about Inception focusing on special effects.
review:
The dream is (sur)real

Doesn't it sound exhilarating to break into a highly secured building, steal top-secret information while everything around you is being blown up and you are in the middle of a deadly gunfire? For you this may be an action-packed dream but for Dominic Cobb it's the hard reality. Well, more or less. Dom Cobb is an extractor meaning that he can enter one's dream and extract information from them and as a perk he gets to blow things up. The best thing is that if he dies he'll wake up unscathed. However, he cannot go back to his home and family as the police believes he killed his wife. The solution for his problems is thrown at him when an influential businessman, Saito, offers to enable him to go home if he takes the job. Saito needs Cobb to do something called 'Inception', he needs Cobb to change the mind of Saito's competitor by placing an idea into his mind. Many team members believe inception is impossible since you need to go deeply into one's subconscious. Planting an idea into someone's mind is therefore extremely difficult because you know that the idea is given to you and isn't your own. Nonetheless, Cobb takes the job and gets a team together. He enters the mind of Robert Fischer, the son of an important business man. However, there is a mysterious lady Dom didn't tell his team about, who could jeopardize the entire plan.

Throughout the entire movie Nolan succeeds in blowing the minds of the audience with thought-provoking scenes, but what keeps you lying awake at night most is the open end. Furthermore the visual effects supervisor did an awesome job on some action-packed scenes like huge explosions on snowy mountains and entire buildings clashing into the sea like icebergs carving of glaciers, it's a pity that you know it's fake. With the idea of Inception Nolan certifies that the most astonishing movies are created within ourselves as we are dreaming, but he sure did an amazing job in making a surreal reality in "Inception". The blending together of all the elements Nolan has used to create this movie , especially the visual and special effects, and the precision that is necessary to create a crown jewel in the department of movie theater, like this one. Not every part works perfectly, the story line could've been largely expanded upon, the history with Cobb's ex-wife is hardly discussed and the action was definitely out of place in some parts. An example is that it is remarkably impossible to hit a 'good guy' in a movie, but these bad guys deserve an Oscar for missing their target, even if you'd try to suck, I doubt you could reproduce their work of art. But what got me to rate this movie 4.5 out of five stars is the fact that it contains hardly any clichés. There is a femme fatale and a guy that got into a whole lot of trouble, but Nolan has put it in such a way that even though there is a love story going on, the emphasize is put on the fact that it ended, done, over with, finito! What is cliché on the other hand is that, like I mentioned before, the 'bad guys' never hit their target and when they do it's the one person that Cobb needs to survive this so he can overcome his complication and go home safely. What makes it so memorable is that it's no normal sci-fi movie, no sci- fi movie is 'normal', but Inception is applicable to what everyone experiences by night, or by day, dreaming. One does it more often than another, but this movie answers some of the questions you'd otherwise not even think about, like 'how did you end up in that dream, as you never remember the beginning of a dream?'

The special effects were what made this movie blown one's mind, especially once you find out that most of the effects are not animated but are performed by the actors ,instead of the all-time stunt-doubles, on screen. The special effects have a lot to do with stunting and acting, and just a little bit of computer generated imagery has been applied, only to enhance and enlarge features in the movie. So what you see is a combination of real life and visual effects.As the movie progresses, you start to see how all the special effects shape the entire sci-fi, action thriller, taking you to different areas of your own imagination. The most beautiful part about the entire story is that nothing like it has ever been done before. When you watch any movie, you do it as entertainment, because you can enter a new world, a world that is not yours, a world that seems to be a dream. But in 'Inception' the people in the movie are in a dream, or aren't they?

Inception is definitely a must see and can without a doubt be described as a masterpiece in the history of film making. It is a movie that you must see more than once to fully grasp it, but it's unquestionably worth the time as you can hardly get bored with this kind of cinematics. In the end, when it's all over and the dream has finished, you'll realize you ended up right in the middle of it and everything you thought you knew turns out to be something entirely different. Because of the combination of the visual effects and the acting, I was captivated by this movie and would therefore, without a single doubt in the world, rate it a 4.5 out of 5 stars.

title: Review
review:
Inception has Leonardo DiCaprio as a "dream thief" who infiltrates and alters other people's dreams, and finds himself caught in a limbo of dream worlds, which the movie tries at considerable length to explain without ever doing much more than parroting the inbred logic of its relentlessly preposterous plot. It's an elaborately pedantic scheme whose lone virtue is that it serves as a good excuse for some bizarre mixtures of action fantasy and special effects. The technical virtuosity pouring from every frame is astounding.The visuals are stunning, perhaps the most fully realized of any film.

Screenwriter/director Christopher Nolan's story mixes fictional dream science and a kind of inner-space espionage, but neither the science nor the espionage matters much here. Mainly it posits a story world in which Leo and company are caught up in dreams within dreams—and eventually a dream within a dream within another dream. But even that aspect of it doesn't really take off, action- and entertainment-wise, until the film is well into its protracted final phases. His tale of purposeful memory-travel is a fun and exciting trip into the creative subconscious. If Inception is a metaphysical puzzle, it's also a metaphorical one: It's hard not to draw connections between Cobb's dream-weaving and Nolan's filmmaking, an activity devoted to constructing a simulacrum of reality.

DiCaprio's Cobb is the Orpheus of Nolan's inner world underground, and Cobb's wife Mal (Marion Cotillard) is its Eurydice. But Page's Ariadne is in some ways the real moral and emotional center of the story, even as Cobb's dilemmas and dreads drive most of the action. Cotillard, playing the film's most oddly conflicted character, comes closest of the group to doing some good character acting, and Joseph Gordon-Levitt is intriguingly mercurial as the best of the film's several sidekicks. Is the best film of the year and one of the best films of the decade, this is Nolan's masterpiece and it is perfect in every regard, the fact that the plot demands attention only adds to the exhilaration. This is a story about dreams that requires the audience to stay awake.

title: Sci-fi Thriller
review:
Writer-director Christopher Nolan explores the realm of dreams in Inception, his first film since his acclaimed box office juggernaut The Dark Knight. The sci-fi thriller's premise sounds simple enough, but its execution by Nolan is anything but. Ostensibly an international heist caper, Inception follows Dom Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), an "extractor" whose form of corporate espionage is to invade the dreams of the rich and powerful and pluck their most tightly guarded secrets from the depths of their subconscious. "A single idea from the human mind can build cities. An idea can transform the world and rewrite all the rules," Cobb says at one point.

Cobb is an international fugitive due to a dark deed from his past that prevents him from being able to return state side to see his children. A shady corporate titan, Mr. Saito (Ken Watanabe), offers Cobb a chance to wipe his past clean and go home. The job? Inception -- planting an idea into a mark's subconscious rather than stealing one. Saito wants Cobb and his longtime point man, Arthur (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), to invade the dreams of Robert Fischer (Cillian Murphy), the heir to an energy conglomerate who is also riddled with daddy issues. Saito wants to take out the competition so to speak.

title: A Fresh, Action Packed, and Thought Provoking Sci-Fi Flick Sure to Please
review:
When I first saw the trailer for Inception on television, I became convinced that Inception was just a bunch of special effects; just another plot-lacking sci-fi flick designed just to please the eyes. The hype around the movie was just too much and it wore on my perception of the movie. Therefore, I didn't go and see it in theaters. Flash forward a month or two to a movie night at my friend's house. They had the DVD of Inception and wanted to watch it. They all said it was great, but I was still skeptical. After a few minutes of watching, I was hooked. The ideas where interesting, the plot was great, and the acting nearly perfect. Inception is now one of my favorite sci-fi movies of all time.

The foremost positive feature of inception is the original plot. Most sci-fi movies these days have to involve either aliens or large robots and generic action scenes. The lack of originality in these movies is quite annoying. Inception however, has the originality desperately needed. The twists and roles the characters play are interesting and create a story that will keep you on your toes. The main character we follow is a man named Cobb (DiCaprio). He has been separated from his family and desperately wants to get back to them. His chance comes in the form of a business offer. A large company run by a man by the name of Saito recruits Cobb and his partner to perform an operation called Inception (a dream with in a dream) to plant an idea in the mind of Saito's chief competitor who is about to inherit his father's company. Cobb is a famous extractor and one of the only people in the world who knows how to do this. Cobb forms a team to complete this risky task with the promise of great rewards. Little do Cobb or his team know that the struggle is about to get more real than ever before. Not only is the plot gripping, but it is also very complex with the different levels of dreams and how they coincide with the different timing of "kicks." In fact, I had to watch this movie twice to really understand exactly how the dreams with in dreams connected with reality. Overall this gripping plot is sure to keep you on your toes and listening to every word the characters mutter or shout.

The acting is extremely well done. Everyone in this movie, from Cobb to the people formed by the dream environment, act in a realistic and convincing way. You can feel the emotions they show. This is not surprising given the list of famous actors in this movie who include Leonardo DiCaprio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, and more.

The action sequences in Inception are very well done. Although they are not as intense as scenes from movies like the Matrix, they are still great. These scenes are almost Bond-like in the way they are scripted and shot, which is quite interesting. The action scenes add an intensity that keeps the movie's pace and adds risk into the dream environment.

Themes and ideas about dreams and how Cobb and his team enter them are thought provoking. What happens when you share dreams? What happens when there is a dream within a dream? These questions are just a few that the film answers. The way that Inception introduces these ideas to you feels natural and makes sense, given our own dreams. It really capitalizes on the believability of the way the dreams are created and the effects experienced in the dreams. Overall, Inception's dream concepts are well implemented and very convincing, which draws people in so they can dream a little themselves.

There is no way I could end this review without mentioning Han Zimmer's amazing sound track. The music fits this movie like a glove. It provides an experience that I haven't really had in any other movie. The emotion evoked during important scenes is compounded with the addition of Zimmer's powerful orchestral assault. If you have a surround sound system, you will experience the full impact of the music in this movie. The booms that coincide with the "kicks" experienced to get a dreamer out of a dream are quite the experience.

Inception is an unforgettable movie experience. Leave behind any biases you may have, forget the hype and gripes or whatever you've heard, and just watch it. I think that you will enjoy it!

title: A real mind-blowing experience featuring Hans Zimmer at his best with an awesome dream-like score.
review:
This is perhaps the most innovative and satisfying blockbuster of the past few years. This means that some scenes were filmed specifically to fit the score rather than the usual other way around, which ends up in one of the best music atmosphere ever created for the big screen.

The directing and cinematography was amazing, and the acting was solid. I can't see anyone else playing Cobb but DiCaprio and he did a fine job. Marion Cotillard and the lovely Ellen Page both did a great job with pretty much the only female roles. Joseph Gordon-Levitt and Tom Hardy had great chemistry together and I hope to see more of them.

You might need a second watch as it is quite a fast-paced movie, and while most of the elements seem to be extensively explained (perhaps one of the only negative things about this movie - the amount of explanation gets annoying upon re-watch), there are definitely some layers that require additional viewings to grasp and acknowledge how well thought this movie really was. If you enjoyed it, I recommend you watch the animated prequel.

It's definitely not for everyone, but it worked very well for me. This is probably my personal favorite movie of the past 10 years.

title: Delivers brains as well as bang for your buck
review:
Inception wasn't the only time English writer-director Christopher Nolan has blown our minds with a big-budget summer blockbuster - two years before, he made The Dark Knight, which destroyed most people's pre- conceptions of what superhero movies should be made of, and showed you that movies designed to make a lot of money can work your brain as much as your heart-rate. Inception also blows the minds of it's characters, themselves barely able to keep up with the multi-level dream universe they create. It's a film that revels in it's own heavy exposition; finding visual thrills in discovering the possibilities of consciously walking through a dream, or showing you the beautiful art of dream- stealing.

It follows Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), an exiled criminal who makes his money from corporate espionage jobs bankrolled by rich CEO's. Only, Cobb applies his craft by entering people's dreams, extracting information left over by the dreamer's subconscious, usually within a locked safe or protected by projections of that subconscious. After a botched job, Cobb's target Saito (Ken Watanabe) offers him the chance to redeem himself and to go home, only the task is not to steal information, but to implant it, known as 'inception'. Saito wants Cobb to implant an idea into the head of Robert Fischer (Cillian Murphy), the heir to an energy conglomerate. Cobb alone has ever achieved inception, but it is a near impossible task, especially with the psychopathic projection of his dead wife (Marion Cotillard) stalking his subconscious.

It's a dangerous and bold thing for a mainstream director to have confidence in it's audiences intelligence. If there's a main problem with Inception, it is probably that things get a little too baffling at times, as the crew delve deeper and deeper into the levels of the dream, and new rules start to apply. There is a lot of information to process here, and the film spends nearly its duration trying to explain it to us. But Nolan is a fantastic writer, and most directors would lose the audience without such expert storytelling ability and great dialogue. Thankfully, Ariadne (Ellen Page), an architecture student recommended to Cobb to design the dream world, plays as a proxy for the audience, learning as we learn.

Ariadne is one of a bunch of experts lined up for the job - Arthur (Joseph Gordon-Levitt) is Cobb's right-hand man and the brains behind the job, Eames (Tom Hardy) is a skilled in-dream impersonator, and Yusuf (Dileep Rao) is a chemist who provides a knockout drug so powerful that the dreamers cannot be shaken awake. There's also Tom Berenger, Michael Caine, Lukas Haas and Pete Postlethwaite in the mix, making this a huge ensemble. As expected, Nolan keeps tabs on them all, never allowing you to forget about anyone or about what the role they have to play. It's a miracle he even managed to line up such an impressive group of actors, let alone make sure no-one gets lost amongst the thick plot.

Although the climax gets a little too over-crowded in the final half an hour, and Nolan places us in the pretty dull setting of a snowy mountain, this is still innovative, stylish and exciting action cinema. It still abides by all the standard rules of the genre, but it dares to toy with them and to keep the action moving with intriguing sub-plots or simply delivering an exceptional set-piece (Arthur's no-gravity hallway fight comes to mind). It bends the mind as much as it bends the rules, and this is much about the strangeness of dreams and what it means to dream them. Nolan went on to deliver an ever better movie two years later with The Dark Knight Rises (2012), and I'm eagerly awaiting his upcoming Interstellar (2014). He alone has reawakened my faith in the 'big' movie, proving that films can deliver brains as well as bang for your buck.

title: Excellent Blending of Two Stories with the same Concept
review:
Christopher Nolan did an excellent job of intertwining two stories together that contained the same concept - Inception. The first story is Leonardo's experience with Inception and the second story is about how a Team facilitates Inception in Robert Fischer, who is the Target.

During the movie, DiCaprio (Dom Cobb) knows full well, that Inception is possible. However, he hides this fact for most of the movie. The meat of the first story is how Leonardo deals with the consequences and ramifications of planting an idea in his wife's mind.

The second story discusses the strategy that the Team will use to plant an idea in the Target's mind and then the second story actually shows them doing it. In a nutshell, the goal of the Team is to plant a pinwheel into a safe which is owned by Robert Fischer's father. Since Robert Fischer treasured a specific photograph which contained the pinwheel, the Team uses this as a means of validating the moment of Inception which they worked so hard to facilitate.

The two stories run parallel with each other throughout the movie and then at the end of the movie both stories present major revelations. In the first story, Inception has already taken place. In the second story, Inception is revealed. In other words, the audience finally comes to understand how Inception influenced DiCaprio throughout the entire film and the the audience also gets to see exactly how the Team architects an elaborate plan to manifest Inception in Robert Fischer - the Target.

The Dream within a Dream within a Dream is a sophisticated metaphor. Don't get overly concerned with trying to track every little movement throughout the layers. And, don't spend too much time worrying about the logic or possible conundrums that this metaphor presents. Enjoy the action and special effects, however, concentrate on the main thrust of the movie which is the notion of how Inception can radically affect and change a person's psyche.

Also, as the movie concludes, contemplate DiCaprio's involvement in the second story. In other words, you will come to appreciate how Nolan used DiCaprio's character to guide the Team with his specific knowledge, while at the same time, coming to grips with his own demons as a result of having already implemented a variation of the ongoing Team strategy in the first story.

title: Inception
review:
The movie Inception directed by Christopher Nolan is outstanding! Movie viewers are consumed by details and innuendos throughout the move. It is consuming, almost an overload for movie watchers; it is mind boggling. Leaving the movie, one feels exhausted from what they just witnessed; what was that? Did you get it? Those were some of the questions I heard from the audience as I was leaving the theater. This movie holds the viewers' hostage; you are glued to the screen. Inception is packed with action, drama, romance, experienced actors, and a complex storyline that has you thinking the entire time.

Inception jumps from one dimension to another. The movie jumps from reality to a "Dream State". At first, it is hard to catch onto what is happening; the action and thrill are intense and gradually elevate to a point where viewers are jumping out of their seats.

Leonardo DeCaprio, Ellen Page, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Tom Hardy, as well as the other actors are excellent! The acting is full of emotion. Each actor is present in scenes that go from love making to furiously attacking one another. Viewers wonder how each person can endure the drama. The actors not only were required to change their emotions but also to be capable of acting mentally ill, physically ill, or physically hurt.

One of the things that made this movie so successful, was the use of special effects throughout the entire movie. The director and special effects team was able to move entire cities upside down. They converted bridges and wall structures from three dimensions to one dimension; they created symmetrical views that mirrored each other. They reversed peoples lives jumping from the present to the past to the future. And they inserted tiny little details, clues, that the astute viewer noticed and added to the mystery and science fiction elements of the movie.

At times the movies is confusing. The attentive viewer realized that the entire movie is a giant mind puzzle. If you aren't into stretching your imagination or able to closely follow a story line, do not see this movie.

The basic storyline is that Dom Cobb (Leonardo Decaprio) is a skilled thief, not a traditional thief but a thief that steals peoples thoughts and ideas. He gets in trouble when he messes around with stealing ideas from powerful people and is identified as a corporate fugitive. He is offered one more chance to redeem himself and this is where the other players come in with the constant mind games and dangers that are present to Dom Cobb. The weird spin to the movie is going from reading peoples minds to learning how to implant ideas into peoples minds. Ideas that they act upon and they are not always good ideas, often for his or others benefit. That sets the storyline.

Once a viewer realized the rules of inception the movie becomes mind boggling and almost curious to attempt or believe inception might actually be possible. The end of the movie is puzzling for one main reason; the audience is left to believe their own opinion of what happened. Most of the time when watching movies I can't stand cliff hangers but, the movie Inception stimulates your thinking and has you leaving the movie theater consumed with thought.

Overall I felt as though the movie Inception was a very well written and planned theatric movie. I enjoyed the mind puzzling situations and how the idea was not completely unrealistic. Christopher Nolan did an outstanding job of not giving away the surprises that lurked around every corner throughout the entire movie. He executed the strategy of having a trail of clues to slightly indicate what would happen next; but just when you think you know BAM, a random surprise occurs. Nolan picked great actors for each character role and uses each of that actors strength to the movies' best interest as well as never expecting more than that actors' own ability.

In my opinion is a fantastic movie that was created by an incredible director! I would most definitely recommend watching this film to my friends as well as anyone who wants their thinking challenged at the movie theater. The plot has left every viewer I know mind boggled and attempting to understand more and more of the video. Inception is a special movie that is fully capable of making viewers have a desire to watch the film more than once. It is a great movie and if a person has not seen it I would highly recommend watching this film on your next movie date or whenever you have some spare time.

title: ehhhhh
review:
The first time I watched this movie, I turned it off about 15 minutes into it. I never even reviewed it or gave it any stars because I didn't think it would be fair to review a movie I hadn't seen.

I turned it off because I thought it was full of nothing but weird, pointless action sequences that fell back on the cliché deux-ex-machina: "And they woke up, and it was all a dream."

After taking the time to watch it (all two and a half hours), I now feel I can give it a review.

I'm giving it five stars because it's not a bad movie, but it's not a great movie either. I can think of several ways this movie can be improved:

1. Starting off from the viewpoint of someone who is just beginning to understand the dream tech. The new architect - whatshername (sorry, bad with names) - is a great choice. She is practically the only strong female character in this movie, so having it from her point of view would help the female audience feel more connected to the storyline in a movie full of male characters.

2. Set clear boundaries. One reason the Matrix had universal appeal and this movie doesn't, is because it had clear boundaries about what the Matrix is and what it is not. Through the eyes of Neo, the audience could learn what was real and what was simulation and how the technology worked. Inception, on the other hand, thrusts the viewer into scene after scene of dreams within dreams within a futuristic reality with no understanding of what is going on or how it is working. Only through bits and pieces can the audience deduce how things work.

3. The technology is ridiculous. Sorry but it is. The whole "needle in the arm" seems like a cop out. Why not put some effort into it, like make it something that looks like an mp3 player that can hook up to the briefcase thingy to share dreams - the earbuds could be acoustics that translate into brainwaves via sound to receive and transmit dream data. Every once in a while, a film comes along that sinks into your collective consciousness, that pushes boundaries that you didn't know could be pushed, that seems to have something for everyone whether you're a fan of complex and intelligent Science-Fiction, or just a plain Action nut.

This movie is Inception. It's a film that redefines what a summer blockbuster can do, and makes you wish for more. A film that makes you think long and hard hours after you left the cinema. A film that effortlessly blends and mixes aspects from all sorts of genres, and makes something wholly new and original come out of the pot.

As a Science-Fiction film, it succeeds by creating a world where it is possible to enter someones dreams, see their thoughts and steal (or incept) ideas from their mind. As an Action film, it succeeds by creating original and exciting set pieces, most notable of the bunch is a breathtaking spinning hallway fight scene that still leaves my jaw dropped every time I see it.

Sure it has it's flaws, like the fact that characters often take a back seat in favor of explaining the rules and physics of this world, and also having some inconsistencies with the rules themselves, but with such a grand and thought provoking concept, it was inevitably going to have some. Most important is the fact that non of the flaws take away from the excitement, the thrills, and the overall fun you experience while watching this fantastic film.

It also holds a special place for me personally, seeing how it is the source of one of my favorite running jokes that i have with my friends. Because the film deals with the idea of dreams within dreams, me and my friends like thinking of funny ideas for "Something within Something" to get "Something-Ception". For example: It's a film, within a film, within a film... Filmception! Try it, the possibilities are limitless.

Christopher Nolan has created yet another masterpiece to his impressive track record, and has created a modern classic for all to enjoy. I give this film a 9/10

title: Facets of a Diamond Dream
review:
Inception is a diamond in the rough of this year's movies. The brilliance of Inception lies in its many facets. And as we shed light on it and peer into its depths, the light just seems to bounce off the facets more and more, giving this diamond a dazzling glow.

The first facet is immediately apparent at the end of the movie, as the screen cuts to black before we see the spinning top fall. We are brought to stark awareness that we did not see the top fall; the top could very go on spinning forever and the 'reality' that the events of the movie are based upon may very well just be another layer of this dream within a dream.

What many people don't realize is that this doubt (that we feel so intellectually gratified at realizing on our own) is the true brilliance of the movie. The very fact that we can draw a conspiracy theory doubting the entire veracity of the movie just based on the ending scene of a slowing down top that we did not see stop completely shows how successful Nolan's inception (I refer to the action of implanting the idea here, rather than the movie) has been. What this means is we ourselves are part of this dream within a dream within a dream within a dream. We ourselves are part of the inception. As Cobb and his team go deeper into the layers of consciousness, we too go with him. And at limbo, that very deepest layer of dream, we are incepted: emotionally, as the drama between Cobb and his wife unfolds; intellectually, pounded into us by shifting of scenes between layers; but most importantly, subconsciously, as the movie begins with limbo.

From the beginning of the movie, we are struck with the question that defines a dream; the very same question that Cobb asks Ariadne: how did we get here? We don't know how things started, even though we are in the thick of action already. We don't know how dream machines come about. We don't know what year it is. We don't know the genesis. Right from the beginning, as we watch Cobb getting washed up upon the shore, our own dream begins. Of course, beginning with the end is a method of inception in itself. By showing us the end, Nolan gives us tainted glasses to watch the movie through. As we watch the movie unfold, we watch it with foreknowledge and prejudice and stereotype. Nolan does to us exactly what he does with the characters in the movie; he infects our tabula rasa with the virus of an idea. He incepts us. And thus, we become part of the dream.

The power of the idea is amplified when we internalize it and when we start to find implications for it. For the danger of an idea is not the idea in itself, but in its repercussions. And if we assimilate these ideas and start to question... do I know my beginning? Do I remember being born? How did I come into this world? We realize, alarmingly, that we don't know. We are as dumbstruck as Ariadne and we realize with chilling possibility that we might be living a dream. That nagging doubt, that gnawing suspicion, that tainted lenses; that is the power of Inception.

Another facet of the movie is the theme of faith. Saito asks Cobb early on in the movie, "Dare you take a leap of faith? Or become an old man, filled with regret, waiting to die alone." And at the end, while we are caught up in figuring whether things were real or not, Cobb has already gone beyond us. He has left the top behind without bothering to see if it stops or not. He cares more about hugging his children then he does about checking whether he is in a dream. He has taken that leap of faith. He has come full circle, despite rejecting Mal's words - "You're waiting for a train. A train that will take you far away. You know where you hope the train will take you, but you can't be sure. But it doesn't matter because we'll be together." It doesn't matter any more whether things are real; what matters is they are together. And in taking that leap of faith, Cobb has taken one step (or leap) further than us, for we are still stuck with our doubts. Cobb, the character in the movie, has gone further than us who are in the real world. The fiction, the fantasy the dream; they have gone further than reality.

And the last facet that I'm going to talk about is that the whole movie being just Nolan's dream. It's a paracosm (credit to posef for this idea) that he created for himself to showcase his sick special effects and awesome directing skills. And from his distinctive non-linear storyline style, multiple levels of meanings and explorations of a myriad of themes at the same time, this movie is somewhat a microcosm of his own mind as well.

And there are many other facets I'm sure; many other ideas spawned by this movie that I have not covered, which other critics will expound on in greater detail. But that's the point, isn't it? Ideas beget ideas. They are viruses, after all. They multiply and consume. That's another facet =)

title: Theme, special effects, and musical score.
review:
Inception (2010), written and directed by Christopher Nolan, takes us through a wild ride of exciting and intriguing action, while at the same time pulling at our heart strings with a confusing and unconventional love story. Dom Cobb, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, possesses a unique ability to extract information from someone's mind while they are dreaming. This ability has put him in a compromising position and brings him to one final mission that is Inception. Cobb is approached by Mr. Saito (Ken Watanabe), to implant an idea into the mind of Robert Michael Fischer, Jr. (Cillian Murphy), the young heir of a business empire. Upon completion of this job, Cobb will get back the life he has lost. Cobb must employ the help of his partner, Arthur (Joseph Gordon-Levitt); associate, Eames (Tom Hardy); and highly recommended architectural student, Ariadne (Ellen Page) to complete a task that is thought to be impossible. The crew encounters a barrage of obstacles, but one in particular wreaks havoc they never expected.

The theme of this movie demonstrates a focus on the complexity of human relationships. Not only does it show the yearning and thirst for love between Cobb and his wife, Mal (Marion Cotillard), but it shows the value and difficulties of having confidence and trust in others. As the crew begins their descent further into the dream world, they soon learn the value of trust. Their journey starts with an ambush by their subject's subconscious. This is their first lesson in trust. The group trusted Arthur to conduct proper research of their subject's history, background, and knowledge of dream infiltration. Not long after, the group is shocked to discover that their mission is even more dangerous than anticipated. Cobb fails to tell them that if things go wrong they could be stuck in the dream world for decades.

Perhaps one of the most valuable off-screen elements of this movie is the soundtrack, written by Hans Zimmer. Nominated for an Academy Award in 2011, the powerful sounds match up perfectly with every scene, intensifying as the drama does. The majority of it intended to mimic Cobb's feelings throughout the film; the viewer is able to connect with the emotional states of longing and desperation that Cobb has.

Nolan also takes advantage of special effects to enhance visual stimulation and to make the viewer feel like they really understand the concept of living in a dream. When Ariadne is first introduced to the dream world, she lets her imagination run wild. We see scenes of a busy city folding in half, moving bridges, and walls made of mirrors representing the metaphor of our dreams having endless possibilities.

Inception is both exciting and intriguing to the viewer. Both cinematic effects and off-screen contributions bring a special addition to the development of the theme. Although slightly outdone by the special effects, the theme represents an excellent example of the complexities in human relationships.

title: Nolan's Best movie again
review:
Inception is truly one of a kind. A concept which has long gestated in Christopher Nolan's mind, his eye for drama mixed with his large scale sensibilities ring true in Blockbuster season making Inception a true original in the sea of reboots, remakes and sequels.

To try and explain Inceptions many plot twists and incredibly intelligent arcs, would be a foolish task. As Nolan himself has been reluctant to. The best way to approach the film would be with an open mind, if you are prepared to be taken on a ride of a lifetime, then trust that you 100% will. If Avatar was a seminal film in technology (although coming out as a rather poor film, in my opinion), then Inception is seminal in it's storytelling. With a 148 minute running time, you would expect a lot to take place, but what you wouldn't expect is the pace of it all. I did not think at one time in the film about how long was left. I was simply blown away by the depth in every single part of the film. If my enthusiasm for the storytelling aspect of the film has left you worried about the spectacle, then don't worry. They are, as hinted in the trailer, incredible, looking real and unbelievable simultaneously. The most pleasing thing about the action set pieces, is that they are genuinely used to illustrate the story, rather than to blow stuff up a la Michael Bay.

With this complex movie in it's high concept, a stellar cast is needed. And Nolan as always, delivers with just that. This is vintage DiCaprio, perhaps only equaled in The Aviator, which is even more impressive as his role as Cobb in Inception is not a showy one, needing DiCaprio to be the constant at the center of the film. And he pulls off Cobb's emotional contradictions sublimely. The rest of the cast members all shine in parts of the films, Cillian Murphy shows off his usually non-existent tender side, Gordon-Levitt bottles his usual charm for his confidently reserved turn as the reliable Arthur, Watanabe is devilish as the seemingly ambiguous Saito, Page shows why she's the next big female star and Tom Hardy revels in being the comic relief of the film compared to his recent turns as decidedly psychopathic characters.

Overall, Nolan has indeed surpassed himself. He has created a world as expansive as his Gotham, a plot dwarfing the intricacies of Memento and one which blows The Prestige's cinematic reveal out of the water. This is truly unmissable cinema. Revel in it, we've still got to wait a whole two years before Batman 3.

title: I cannot recommend this film anymore than I have, I just have to say everyone and anyone should see it. Sorry about all the gushing, it is just so hard not too...
review:
Usually I try to be careful with over hyping a film, or setting the expectations too high, as film geeks all are guilty for, however for Christopher Nolan's Inception, this really is not possible.

This is possibly one of the only perfect films I have ever seen. It is absolutely confident in every way, something which is extremely refreshing, even more so than Avatar. Christopher Nolan gets some slack for making great to look at but ultimately heartless affairs, which I for one do not agree with, however I do not think anyone can argue that here. The emotional aspect of this film not only ties it all together but is really the center of this film, it is the focus.

I do not want to over simplify the film, by simply calling it Kubrick doing Bond, or Gondry on a huge budget, because I am sure it will be called that but it is far more than that, it is something I do not think Kubrick could have ever made. It is pure Nolan, and pure greatness.

I hate writing something which is pure fan-boy gushing, but its really difficult here. I did not find a thing I did not like about it, I am sure if maybe I saw it a second time, maybe I would find something about it I didn't like, but not the first time. The way it is cut, means that there is always action on screen, if not, then the visuals are interesting enough to keep your eyes glued.

The final hour of the film, is possibly one of the most complicated action sequences put on film. You have to constantly be paying attention to remember all of the layers of what is happening. Without spoiling anything, all I have to say is that is what this film is about, that is what makes this film so great, layers. Once you have seen this you will now what I am talking about.

All of the actors are fantastic too, Di Caprio is the stand out here. Yes, this is probably due to the fact he is the star and given all of the emotional weight, but he handles it perfectly, similarly to his performance in Shutter Island. Ellen Page, whom I usually hate, gives a great performance here. Tom Hardy gives a break out performance here, he is quite the bad ass.

I hope audiences are ready for a film like this, a pure auteur driven film which does not sacrifice a single frame for the studio. I would hope this film will change Hollywood, as it is 100 percent the directors vision yet it is definitely a marketable film, much like District 9, yet I do not think it will.

title: Excellently Executed and Engaging
review:
Start with a simple idea, and let it grow naturally in a persons mind until they are consumed by the concept. This is the basic premise of Christopher Nolan's 2010 film, Inception. Leonardo DiCaprio leads the cast featuring names such as Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Tom Hardy, Ellen Page and Cilian Murphy. The team (DiCaprio, Gordon-Levitt, Hardy and Page) are hired to plant an idea in a business mans (Murphy) mind through his dreams. There are plenty of twists and turns in the complex scheme which evolves throughout the story. The dangers of being killed in the dream, being discovered by the dreamers subconscious and being followed by DiCaprio's own image of his dead wife (Marion Cottilard) are constantly in mind as the group travels deeper and deeper into the maze of dreams upon dreams until they reveal the possibility of falling into limbo.

An engrossing concept and complex plot structure makes the film amusing to think about, however it also opens the script up to a few minor inconsistencies now and again. The script is overall very well paced. The story is well set up, and the tone is established equally well. Cinematography and special effects in the dream sequences are phenomenal. The images and scenery manipulation involved becomes another character in itself.

The score for the film is memorable and recognizable. The only downside to the musical background is that there are a few moments where the music is overpowering and overplayed in the scene. The delivery of the script is as impressive as the concept that it began with. The actors deliver the dialogue capably and with great timing. Ellen Page seems a bit monotonous at times which takes away from the dialogue. Hardy and Gordon-Levitt play off of each other in a way that offers breaks in the tension, but it also leaves the serious tone well established. DiCaprio and Murphy are the two stand outs as far as the acting goes. While I am not a big Leo fan, I must admit that without him in this role the film could have fallen apart at the seams.

The concept which the movie delves into is amusing to think about even after the film ends. It almost parallels the way movies work. An audience watches a film, and a scene or line becomes lodged in the viewers mind. As time passes they are reminded of the main idea and an emotion develops from that. Before there is any time to realize what has happened, that idea becomes truth to the viewer. This movie is worth seeing for any person interested in thought provoking films as well as any action fans.
